2107.text: Acrosome reaction in sperm is triggered by
2107.sol: The activated spermatozoan on reaching the egg plasma membrane, undergoes a number of changes in its acrosomal region. All these changes are collectively described under acrosome reaction. Calcium influx may activate phospholipase resulting in accumulation of unsaturated fatty acids and fusiogenic lysophospholipids contributing to acrosome reaction.

5100.text: Analysis shows that nickel oxide has the formula $\mathrm{Ni}_{0.98} \mathrm{O}_{1.00}$. The fractions $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Ni}^{3+}$ ions in the crystal are......
5100.sol:
It is given that, nickel oxide has the formula as $\mathrm{Ni}_{0.98} \mathrm{O}_{1.00}$.
As per the formula, there are $98 \mathrm{Ni}$ ions for 100 oxide ions. Out of $98 \mathrm{Ni}$ ions, let $x$ ions be in +2 oxidation state.
$(98-x)$ ions will be in +3 oxidation state.
Oxide ion has -2 charge.
To maintain electrical neutrality, total positive charge on cations = total negative charge on anions. $\begin{aligned}2 x+3(98-x)+100(-2) \text{ and } =0 \\
x \text{ and } =94
\end{aligned} Fraction of \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ions =$\frac{94}{98}=$0.96Fraction of $\mathrm{Ni}^{3+} ions =\frac{4}{98}$=$0.04$
Hence, the fractions of nickel that exists as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+} and \mathrm{Ni}^{3+}$ are $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}=96 \%$ and $\mathrm{Ni}^{3+}=4 \%$ respectively.

6215.subject: Mathematics
6215.text: The diameter and altitude of a right circular cone, at a certain instant, were found to be $10$ cm and $20$ cm respectively. If its diameter is increasing at a rate of $2cm / s$, then at what rate must its altitude change, in order to keep its volume constant?
6215.sol:
Let $D$ is diameter, $h$ is altitude and $r$~is radius of the right circular cone.

$\dfrac{dD}{dt} = 2cm / s$

$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 1cm / s$

$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pir^{2}h$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\dfrac{d\left(r^{2}h\right)}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \lleft(r^{2}\dfrac{dh}{dt} ++2r\dfrac{dr}{dt} \timesh\right)

$0 = $\dfrac{π}{3} \lleft(25\dfrac{dh}{dt} +10 $\times$20 $\times$1\right)$

$0 = 25\dfrac{dh}{dt} +200$

$\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -8cm / s$.

6234.text: The difference between the greatest and least values of the function $f ( x ) = - x + sin2x$ on~$\left[- \dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$ is
6234.sol:
$f ( x ) = - x + sin2x$

in~$\left[- \dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$

$f^{'} ( x ) = 2cos2x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{π}{6}$

$f ( x )$~increasing in& $x \in \left[- \dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{π}{6}\right]

decreasing in~$x \in $\left[- \dfrac{π}{2}, - \dfrac{π}{6}\right] ∪ \left[\dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$

$\left(f ( x )\right)maximum$~at& $x = - \dfrac{π}{2}$~or& $\dfrac{π}{6}$

$f\left(- \dfrac{π}{2}\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$\left(f ( x )\right)minimum$~at& $x = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$f\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = - \dfrac{π}{2}$

So,~$\dfrac{π}{2} + \dfrac{π}{2} = \pi$

7142.text: If $x-y+1=0$ meets the circle $x^2+y^2+y-1=0$ at $A$ and $B$, then the equation of the circle with $A B$ as diameter is
7142.sol:
Given that circle, $S=x^2+y^2+y-1=0$
Line, $\mathrm{L}: x-y+1=0$
Equation of the circle passing through the intersection of line and circle is given by
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{S}+\lambda \mathrm{L}=0 \\
& \left(x^2+y^2+y-1\right)+\lambda(x-y+1)=0 \\
& x^2+y^2+\lambda x+(1-\lambda) y+\lambda-1=0
\end{aligned}$
Centre of above circle $= \left(\frac{-\lambda}{2}, \frac{\lambda-1}{2}\right)
Since, centre lies on $ x-y+1=0\therefore \quad $\frac{-\lambda}{2}-\left(\frac{\lambda-1}{2}\right)+1=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{3}{2}
Now,$ the $required equation of circle
 \begin{aligned}$& x²+y²+y-1+$\frac{3}{2}($ x-y+1)=0 \\
& \therefore \quad 2 $\left( x^2+y²\right)+3 x-y+1=0
\end{aligned}$

Assertion (A)

7750.sol:
Assertion
Let $I=\int_2^e\left(\frac{1}{\log _e x}-\frac{1}{\left(\log _e x\right)^2}\right) d x$
Let $\log _e x=y$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad x & =e^y \\
\Rightarrow \quad d x & =e^y d y \\
I & =\int_{\log _e 2}^1 e^y\left[\frac{1}{y}+\left(\frac{-1}{y^2}\right)\right] d y
\end{aligned}
$$
[Using the formula $\int_a^b e^x\left[f(x)+f^{\prime}(x)\right] d x=\left[e^x f(x)\right]_a^b$ ]
$$
\begin{aligned}
I & =\left[e^y \frac{1}{y}\right]_{-\log e^2}^1 \\
& =e-\frac{2}{\log _e 2}=e-2 \log _2 e
\end{aligned}
$$
Hence, Assertion and Reason both are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

10002.text: The slopes of the lines represented by $x^2+2 h x y+2 y^2=0$ are in the ratio $(1: 2)$, then $h$ is equal
10002.sol:
Given, equation of lines
$x^2+2 h x y+2 y^2=0...(i)$
On comparing with $a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2=0\Rightarrow \quad a=1$ and $b=2$

From Eq. (ii), we get $m_1+m_2=-h$ and from Eq. (iii) we get
$\begin{array}{llrl}m_1+2 m_1=-h & \text{ and } & m_1 m_2 & =\frac{1}{2} \\ m_1=-h / 3 & \text{ and } & 2 m_1^2 & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow-\frac{h}{3}=\pm \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow h= \pm \frac{3}{2} & \text{ and } & m_1 & =\frac{ \pm 1}{2}\end{array}$

13843.text: A bullet of mass $10g$ pierces through a plate $A$ of mass $500g$ and then gets embedded into a second plate $B$ of mass $1. 49kg$ as shown in the figure. Initially the two plates $A$ and $B$ are at rest and move with same velocity after collision. The percentage loss in the initial kinetic energy of the bullet when it is between the plates $A$ and $B$ is_______. (Neglect any loss of material of the plates during the collision)
13843.sol:
Let us suppose that the mass of the bullet is,& $m = 10g = {10}^{- 2}kg$ and& ${M}_{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}kg, {M}_{B} = 1 . 49kg$,

now the loss of kinetic energy of a bullet is,

$∆ K . E . \times 100 = - \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m{v1}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}} \times 100\right) = - \left(\dfrac{{v1}^{2} - u^{2}}{u2} \times 100\right) ∆ K . E . \times 100 = - \left(\dfrac{{v}_{1}2}{u2} - 1\right) \times 100$

for plate $A$ conservation of momentum,

$mu = m{v}_{1} + {M}_{A}v ⇒ m\left(u - {v}_{1}\right) = {M}_{A}v$

for the plate, $B$ the bullet is combined with plate,

$m{v}_{1} = \left(m + {M}_{B}\right)v$

now from above two-equation of plates,

$\dfrac{u - {v}_{1}}{v1} = \dfrac{MA}{m + {M}_{B}} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{0 . 01 + 1 . 49} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{1 . 50} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$3u - 3{v}_{1} = {v}_{1} ⇒ {v}_{1} = \dfrac{3}{4}u$

$∆ K . E . \times 100 = - \left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}u\right)2}{u2} - 1\right) \times 100 = 43 . 75 %$

15333.text: Which of the following is not true about vectors $\overset{→}{A}, \overset{→}{B}$ and $\overset{→}{C}$?
15333.sol:
Dot/Scalar product of two vectors gives scalar result. Cross/Vector product will give vector result.

Case:& $\left(\overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{→}{A}\right) \left(\overset{→}{B} \cdot \overset{→}{C}\right)

Both left & right part will be a scalar value$ and hence its product will also be a scalar value.

Case: $\left(\overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)$\cdot $\left(\overset{→}{B} \times \overset{→}{C}\right)$

Both left and $right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo dot product and the result will be a scalar value.

Case: \left(\overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{C}\right)$\times $\left(\overset{→}{B} \times \overset{→}{C}\right)$<$/p>

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

Case: $\overset{→}{A} \times $\left(\overset{→}{B} \times \overset{→}{C}\right)$

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

16009.text: A hydrometer executes simple harmonic motion when it is pushed down vertically in a liquid of density $ρ$. If the mass of hydrometer is $m$ and the radius of the hydrometer tube is $r$, then the time period of oscillation is
16009.sol:
If the hydrometer were in equilibrium or floating, its weight will be balanced by the buoyancy force acting on it by the fluid. During its small oscillation, let us locate the hydrometer when it is a vertically downward distance $x$ from its equilibrium position.

Here, the net unbalanced force on the hydrometer is the excess buoyancy force directed upward.

Thus, ${F}_{b} = ρVg = ρ\pir^{2}xg$.

Now, restoring force $ma = {F}_{b}$. So, restoring acceleration is $a = - \dfrac{ρ\pir^{2}gx}{m}$.

For SHM, acceleration is $a = - {ω}^{2}x$.

Then, we have, ${ω}^{2} = \dfrac{ρ\pir^{2}g}{m}$.

Thus, the time period of oscillation is $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\pir^{2}ρg}}$.

17961.subject: Mathematics
17961.text: The points at which the tangent passes through the origin for the curve $y=4 x^{3}-2 x^{5}$ are
17961.sol:
The equation of the given curve is

$\begin{array}{l}

y=4 x^{3}-2 x^{5} \\

\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=12 x^{2}-10 x^{4}

\end{array}$

Therefore,$ the slope of the tangent at point(x, y)$ is $12 x^{2}-10 x^{4}$. The equation of the tangent at $(x, y)$ is given by

$\mathrm{Y}-y=\left(12 x^{2}-10 x^{4}\right)(\mathrm{X}$-$x) \ldots \text{ (i) }$
When,$ the tangent passes through the origin(0,0)$, then  $\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Y}$=$0Therefore, eq. (i) reduce to $\begin{array}{l}

-y=$\left(12 x^{2}-10 x^{4}\right)(-x) \\

\Rightarrow y=12 x^{3}-10 x^{5}

\end{array}$

Also, we have $y=4 x^{3}-2 x^{5}$\begin{array}{l}

\therefore 12 x^{3}-10 x^{5} \\

=4 x^{3}-2 x^{5} \\

\Rightarrow 8 x^{5}-8 x^{3}=0 \\

\Rightarrow x^{5}-x^{3}=0 \\

\Rightarrow x^{3}$\left(x^{2}-1\right)$=0 \\

\Rightarrow x=0, \pm 1

\end{array}$

When, $x=0y=4(0)^{3}-2(0)^{5}=0$

When, $x=1$,

$y=4(1)^{3}-2(1)^{5}=2$

When, $x=-1$,

$y=4(-1)^{3}-2(-1)^{5}=-2$

Hence, the require points are $(0,0),(1,2) and (-1,-2)$.$

20075.subject: Chemistry
20075.text:
The metallic ions that have almost same spin only magnetic moment are :
(i) $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$
(iii) $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$
20075.sol: The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M., where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.For $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ (Z=27$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^7$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. Thus, \mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ B.M.For $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ (Z=25$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^5$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. Thus, \mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ B.M.For $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ (Z=24$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^4$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. Thus, \mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ B.M.For $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ (Z=24$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^3$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. Thus, \mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ B.M.Comparing the calculated magnetic moments, $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ both have $n=3$ unpaired electrons and consequently the same spin-only magnetic moment of $\sqrt{15} B.M.Answer: \text{ (i)$ and (iv) }

20168.subject: Chemistry
20168.text: If electrolysis of water is carried out for a time duration of 2 hours, how much electric current in amperes would be required to liberate $100 \mathrm{ ml}$ of $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas measured under standard conditions of temperature and pressure?
20168.sol:
The electrolysis of water produces oxygen gas at the anode according to the reaction: $2H_2O(l) \rightarrow O_2(g) + 4H^{+}(aq) + 4e^{-}$.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $4$ moles of electrons are required to produce $1$ mole of $O_2$ gas. At standard temperature and pressure (STP), $1$ mole of any gas occupies $22.4$ liters or $22400$ ml.

The volume of $O_2$ given is $100$ ml. The number of moles of $O_2$ produced is $n_{O_2} = \dfrac{100}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{224}$ moles.

The total charge $Q$ required is $n_{e^{-}} \times F$, where $n_{e^{-}} = 4 \times n_{O_2} = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{224} = \dfrac{1}{56}$ moles of electrons and $F = 96500$ C/mol.

$Q = \dfrac{96500}{56} \approx 1723.21$ Coulombs.

The time duration is $2$ hours, which is $2 \times 3600 = 7200$ seconds.

The current $I$ is given by $I = \dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{1723.21}{7200} \approx 0.2393$ A.

Answer: 0.2393 A

20777.subject: Chemistry
20777.text: A certain orbital having 2 angular nodes and no radial nodes is:
20777.sol:
The number of angular nodes in an orbital is given by the azimuthal quantum number $l$.

The number of radial nodes in an orbital is given by the formula $n - l - 1$, where $n$ is the principal quantum number.

Given that the orbital has 2 angular nodes, we have $l = 2$. This corresponds to a d-orbital.

Given that the orbital has 0 radial nodes, we have $n - l - 1 = 0$.

Substituting $l = 2$ into the radial node equation: $n - 2 - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow n = 3$.

Therefore, the orbital is $3d$.

Answer: 3 d

21874.subject: Mathematics
21874.text:
Advika chooses one of three scarves every morning: Red, Blue, or Green.
• The probability she chooses Red is 20%.
• The probability she chooses Blue is twice the probability of choosing Red.
• On the remaining days she wears a Green scarf.
Once a scarf is chosen, she decides whether to wear a Hat (H) and Sunglasses (S). These choices are independent of each other but depend on the scarf colour:
Scarf colourP(H)P(S)
Red0.50.8
Blue0.40.5
Green0.10.5
Advika is spotted outdoors wearing both a Hat and Sunglasses. What is the probability that she is wearing the Red scarf?
21874.sol:
Let $R$, $B$, and $G$ be the events of choosing Red, Blue, and Green scarves respectively.

$P(R) = 0.2$
$P(B) = 2 \times 0.2 = 0.4$
$P(G) = 1 - (0.2 + 0.4) = 0.4$

Let $E$ be the event of wearing both a Hat and Sunglasses. Since the choices are independent for a given scarf:
$P(E|R) = P(H|R) \times P(S|R) = 0.5 \times 0.8 = 0.4$
$P(E|B) = P(H|B) \times P(S|B) = 0.4 \times 0.5 = 0.2$
$P(E|G) = P(H|G) \times P(S|G) = 0.1 \times 0.5 = 0.05$

Using Bayes' theorem, the required probability is:
$P(R|E) = \dfrac{P(E|R)P(R)}{P(E|R)P(R) + P(E|B)P(B) + P(E|G)P(G)}$

$P(R|E) = \dfrac{0.4 \times 0.2}{0.4 \times 0.2 + 0.2 \times 0.4 + 0.05 \times 0.4}$

$P(R|E) = \dfrac{0.08}{0.08 + 0.08 + 0.02}$

$P(R|E) = \dfrac{0.08}{0.18} = \dfrac{4}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{9}$

23143.subject: Physics
23143.text: The speeds of air-flow on the upper and lower surfaces of a wing of an aeroplane $arefv_1$ and $v_2$, respectively. If $A$ is the cross-sectional area of the wing and $\rho$ is the density of air, then the upward lift is
23143.sol:
Due to the specific shape of wings, when the aeroplane runs, air passes at higher speed over it as compared to its lower surface. This difference of air speeds above and below the wings, in accordance with Bernoulli's principle, creates a pressure difference, due to which an upward force called 'dynamic lift' acts on the plate.
$\therefore$ Upward lift $=$ pressure difference $\times$ area of the wings
$[\because F=p \times A]$
From Bernoulli's equation,
$\begin{aligned}
p_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1{ }^2 & =p_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2{ }^2 \\
\because \quad p_2-p_1 & =\frac{1}{2} \rho\left(v_1{ }^2-v_2{ }^2\right) \\
\text{ Hence, upward lift } & =\frac{1}{2} \rho A\left(v_1^2-v_2^2\right)
\end{aligned}$

23439.subject: Physics
23439.text: An object of mass $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ is allowed to hang tangentially from the rim of the wheel of radius R. When released from the rest, the block falls vertically through $4 \mathrm{ m}$ height in 2 seconds. The moment of inertia is $1 \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ m}^2$. The radius of the wheel $\mathrm{R}$ is
23439.sol:
Let $m = 1 \text{ kg}$ be the mass of the block, $I = 1 \text{ kg m}^2$ be the moment of inertia of the wheel, $R$ be the radius of the wheel, and $h = 4 \text{ m}$ be the distance fallen in time $t = 2 \text{ s}$.

The block starts from rest, so the distance fallen is given by $h = \dfrac{1}{2} a t^2$, where $a$ is the linear acceleration of the block.

$4 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times a \times (2)^2 \Rightarrow 4 = 2a \Rightarrow a = 2 \text{ m/s}^2$.

The equation of motion for the block is $mg - T = ma$, where $T$ is the tension in the string.

$1 \times 9.8 - T = 1 \times 2 \Rightarrow T = 9.8 - 2 = 7.8 \text{ N}$.

The torque $\tau$ on the wheel is $\tau = T \times R = I \alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the angular acceleration of the wheel. Since the string does not slip, $a = R \alpha$, so $\alpha = \dfrac{a}{R}$.

$T \times R = I \times \dfrac{a}{R} \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{I a}{R^2}$.

Substituting the known values: $7.8 = \dfrac{1 \times 2}{R^2} \Rightarrow R^2 = \dfrac{2}{7.8} \approx 0.256$.

Using $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$ as a standard approximation in such problems: $10 - T = 2 \Rightarrow T = 8 \text{ N}$.

$8 = \dfrac{1 \times 2}{R^2} \Rightarrow R^2 = \dfrac{2}{8} = 0.25 \Rightarrow R = 0.5 \text{ m}$.

Answer: 0.5 m

Step 1: Identification of monomer $\textbf{X}$
The given reaction sequence for $\textbf{X}$ is:

$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$

$\text{BrCH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3 \text{ (excess)}} \text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$
Thus, $\textbf{X}$ is Glycine.
Molar mass of $\textbf{X}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2$) = $2(12) + 5(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 75 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 2: Identification of monomer $\textbf{Y}$
Caprolactam on acidic hydrolysis gives $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid:
Caprolactam $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{H}_2\text{N}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{COOH}$
Thus, $\textbf{Y}$ is $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid.
Molar mass of $\textbf{Y}$ ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{NO}_2$) = $6(12) + 13(1) + 14 + 2(16) = 131 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 3: Calculation of the mass of copolymer $\textbf{Z}$
The copolymer $\textbf{Z}$ is Nylon-2-nylon-6, which is a biodegradable polyamide formed by the condensation polymerization of Glycine and $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid.
The problem states that $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{X}$ and $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{Y}$ completely react to form $1 \text{ mol}$ of a single acyclic copolymer $\textbf{Z}$.
This means each molecule of polymer $\textbf{Z}$ contains $500$ units of $\textbf{X}$ and $500$ units of $\textbf{Y}$, making a total of $1000$ monomer units.
In an acyclic chain of $1000$ monomers, the number of peptide (amide) bonds formed is $1000 - 1 = 999$.
For each peptide bond formed, one molecule of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is eliminated. Since $1 \text{ mol}$ of polymer $\textbf{Z}$ is formed, $999 \text{ mol}$ of water are eliminated.

Applying the law of conservation of mass:
Mass of $\textbf{Z}$ = (Mass of $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{X}$) + (Mass of $500 \text{ mol}$ of $\textbf{Y}$) - (Mass of $999 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = (500 \times 75) + (500 \times 131) - (999 \times 18)$
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = 37500 + 65500 - 17982$
Mass of $\textbf{Z} = 103000 - 17982 = 85018 \text{ g}$

Answer: $85018$

25447.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ be real numbers such that the system of linear equations
\\ $\begin{array}{c}$\\ x+2 y+3 z=$\alpha$\\ \\ 4 x+5 y+6 z=$\beta$\\ \\ 7 x+8 y+9 z=$\gamma-$1 \\ \end{array} \\ \\ is consistent. Let $|M|$ represent the determinant of the matrix \\ \\ M=$\left[\begin{array}{ccc}$\\ $\alpha$& 2 & $\gamma$\\ \\ $\beta$& 1 & 0 \\ \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ \end{array}\right] \\ \\ Let $P$ be the plane containing all those $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ for which the above system of linear equations is consistent, and $D$ be the square of the distance of the point $(0,1,0)$ from the plane $P$.

The value of $| M |$ is
25447.sol:
$x + 2y + 3z = \alpha$

$4x + 5y + 6z = \beta$

$7x + 8y + 9z = \gamma - 1$

The system of linear equations is consistent it means it has unique solution or infinite solutions

Here, $\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Hence, there are infinitely many solutions.

If equations have infinitely many solutions, then the equations are linearly connected, i.e., ${L}_{1} + \lambda{L}_{2} = {L}_{3}$

$⇒ \left(x + 2y + 3z - \alpha\right) + \lambda ( 4x + 5y + 6z - \beta ) = 7x + 8y + 9z - \gamma + 1$

$\dfrac{1 + 4\lambda}{7} = \dfrac{2 + 5\lambda}{8} = \dfrac{3 + 6\lambda}{9} = \dfrac{\alpha + \lambda\beta}{\gamma - 1}$

$\dfrac{1 + 4\lambda}{7} = \dfrac{2 + 5\lambda}{8} ⇒ \lambda = - 2$

Also,$\dfrac{1 + 4\lambda}{7} = \dfrac{\alpha + \lambdaB}{\gamma - 1}$

$⇒ - 1 = \dfrac{\alpha - 2\beta}{r - 1}$

$⇒ \alpha - 2\beta + \gamma = 1$

Now, $\left|M\right| = \left|\begin{cases}\alpha & 2 & \gamma \\ \beta & 1 & 0 \\ - 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \alpha + 2 ( - \beta ) + \gamma ( 1 ) = \alpha - 2\beta + \gamma = 1$

${PF}_{5}, {BrF}_{5}, {PCl}_{5}, {\left[{PtCl}_{4}\right]}^{2 -}, {BF}_{3}, Fe ( CO{)}_{5}$

${PF}_{5}$ involves sp3d hybridisation and hence has trigonal bipyramidal structure.

In ${PCl}_{5}$  the central atom is surrounded by five bond pairs and no lone paris.
Hybridisation of central atom in ${PCl}_{5}$ molecule is sp3d giving trigonal bipyramidal shape.

In $\left[Fe ( CO{)}_{5}\right]$, oxidation state of CO is zero.

It has hybridisation =dsp3.

So it has trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

${BrF}_{5};$ square pyramidal

${\left[{PtCl}_{4}\right]}^{- 2};$ square planar

${BF}_{3};$ Trigonal planar.

Hence the answer is $3$

32528.subject: Chemistry
32528.text:
Arrange the following isothermal processes in order of the magnitude of the work ($p - V$) involved between states $1$ and $2$.
A. Expansion in single stage $w_A$
B. Expansion in multi stages $w_B$
C. Compression in single stage $w_C$
D. Compression in multi stages $w_D$

Choose the correct option.
32528.sol:
Let State $1$ have pressure $P_1$ and volume $V_1$, and State $2$ have pressure $P_2$ and volume $V_2$. For an isothermal expansion, $V_2 > V_1$ and $P_1 > P_2$.

For expansion from State $1$ to State $2$:
In a single-stage expansion, the external pressure is constant at the final pressure $P_2$. The magnitude of work is $|w_A| = P_2(V_2 - V_1)$.
In a multi-stage expansion, the external pressure is reduced in steps, keeping it closer to the internal pressure of the gas. The work done by the gas increases with the number of stages, reaching a maximum for a reversible process ($|w_{rev}|$). Thus, $|w_{rev}| > |w_B| > |w_A|$.

For compression from State $2$ to State $1$:
In a single-stage compression, the external pressure is constant at the final pressure $P_1$. The magnitude of work is $|w_C| = P_1(V_2 - V_1)$.
In a multi-stage compression, the external pressure is increased in steps. The work done on the gas decreases with the number of stages, reaching a minimum for a reversible process ($|w_{rev}|$). Thus, $|w_C| > |w_D| > |w_{rev}|$.

Since $P_1 > P_2$, the single-stage compression work $|w_C|$ is the largest, and the single-stage expansion work $|w_A|$ is the smallest. The reversible work magnitude $|w_{rev}|$ is the same for both expansion and compression between the same states.

Combining these inequalities, we get:
$|w_C| > |w_D| > |w_{rev}| > |w_B| > |w_A|$

Therefore, the correct order of the magnitude of work is $|w_C| > |w_D| > |w_B| > |w_A|$.

Answer: $|w_C| > |w_D| > |w_B| > |w_A|$

33760.text: Let $z$ be the complex number satisfying $|z-5| \leq 3$ and having maximum positive principal argument. Then $34\left|\frac{5 z-12}{5 \mathrm{i} z+16}\right|^{2}$ is equal to :
33760.sol:
The region $|z - 5| \le 3$ is a disk centered at $(5, 0)$ with radius 3. Maximum positive principal argument from origin occurs at the tangent point from origin to the circle.
$\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$, $\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}$.
The tangent point is the foot of perpendicular from $(5,0)$ to the line $3x - 4y = 0$, giving $z = \frac{16}{5} + \frac{12}{5}i$.
$5z - 12 = 4 + 12i \Rightarrow |5z - 12|^2 = 160$
$5iz + 16 = 4 + 16i \Rightarrow |5iz + 16|^2 = 272$
$34\left|\frac{5z-12}{5iz+16}\right|^2 = 34 \times \frac{160}{272} = 34 \times \frac{10}{17} = 20$.

34188.text: The value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{xdx}{\sin^{4}\left(2x\right) + \cos^{4}\left(2x\right)}$ equals:
34188.sol:
Let, $\mathop{I = ∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{xdx}{\sin^{4}\left(2x\right) + \cos^{4}\left(2x\right)}$

Let, $2x = t$ then $dx = \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{tdt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right)dt}{\sin^{4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right) + \cos^{4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right)}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{\pi}{2}dt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t} - I$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{dt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t}$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{{sec}^{4}tdt}{\tan^{4}t + 1}$

Let, $tant = y$ then ${sec}^{2}tdt = dy$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{\left(1 + {y}^{2}\right)dy}{1 + {y}^{4}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{16}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}}{{y}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{y}^{2}}}dy$

Putting, $y - \dfrac{1}{y} = p$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{16}\mathop{∫}_{- \infty}^{\infty}\dfrac{dp}{{p}^{2} + {\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi}{16\sqrt{2}}{\left[\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{p}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right]}_{- \infty}^{\infty}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{\pi}^{2}}{32}$

38565.text: Let $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}$ be two vectors such that ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$ and ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 75$. Then ${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to ______.
38565.sol:
Given,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$

We know that

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

Now using the above formula in ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$ we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

Now on comparing both side we get, ${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 6 . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right) = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - {\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2} = 75$

Now putting the value of ${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 6$ we get, $6{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} - 9 = 75 ⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 14$

40276.text: A plane electromagnetic wave is moving in free space with velocity $c=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and its electric field is given as $\vec{E}=54 \sin (k z-\omega t) \hat{j} \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}$, where $\hat{j}$ is the unit vector along $y$-axis. The magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ of the wave is:
40276.sol:
For an electromagnetic wave, the relationship between electric and magnetic field amplitudes is $B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c}$.
Here $E_0 = 54$ V/m and $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s.
So, $B_0 = \frac{54}{3 \times 10^8} = 1.8 \times 10^{-7}$ T.
The electric field is along the $\hat{j}$ direction.
Since the wave travels in the $+z$ direction, the magnetic field direction is determined by $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ pointing in the $+z$ direction.
Using the right-hand rule: $\hat{j} \times (-\hat{i}) = \hat{k}$ (positive $z$ direction), confirming the magnetic field is in the $-\hat{i}$ direction.
Therefore, $\vec{B} = -1.8 \times 10^{-7}\sin(kz - \omega t)\hat{i}$ T.

40885.text:
Assume that the earth is a solid sphere of uniform density and a tunnel is dug along its diameter throughout the earth. It is found that when a particle is released in this tunnel, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The mass of the particle is $100g$. The time period of the motion of the particle will be (approximately)

(take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$, radius of earth $= 6400km$)
40885.sol:
The gravitational force acting on a particle of mass $m$ at a distance$r ( < R )$ from the centre of Earth is

$F = - G\dfrac{{M}^{'}m}{{r}^{2}}$ ....(1)

where ${M}^{'}$ is the mass of portion of Earth enclosed by a sphere of radius $r$ concentric with Earth. Here $-$ sign indicates radially inward direction of force.

Taking the density of Earth to be uniform

$\dfrac{{M}^{'}}{4{\pi r}^{3}} = \dfrac{M}{4{\pi R}^{3}}$

$⇒ {M}^{'} = \dfrac{M{r}^{3}}{{R}^{3}}$ ....(2)

Substituting ${M}^{'}$ from equation 2 into equation 1:

$F = - \left(\dfrac{GMm}{{R}^{3}}\right)r$

41087.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I :The average momentum of a molecule in a sample of an ideal gas depends on temperature.

Statement II : The rms speed of oxygen molecules in a gas is $v$. If the temperature is doubled and the oxygen molecules dissociate into oxygen atoms, the rms speed will become $2v$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
41087.sol:
Momentum is a vector quantity and average momentum of molecules of a sample is zero due to random motion.

${P}_{avg} = 0$

RMS speed of a molecule is given by

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Now the temperature is doubled ${T}_{new} = 2T$ and due to dissociation ${M}_{new} = \dfrac{M}{2}$.

$⇒ \dfrac{{v}_{new}}{v} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{2T}{\dfrac{M}{2}}}}{\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{M}}}$

$⇒ {v}_{new} = 2v$

42495.subject: Physics
42495.sol:
For the nucleus $^{209}_{83}Bi$, the number of protons is $Z = 83$ and the number of neutrons is $N = 209 - 83 = 126$.

Mass of $83$ protons $= 83 \times 1.007825 = 83.649475 \, u$

Mass of $126$ neutrons $= 126 \times 1.008665 = 127.091790 \, u$

Total mass of the nucleons $= 83.649475 + 127.091790 = 210.741265 \, u$

The mass defect $\Delta m$ is given by:

$\Delta m = \text{Total mass of nucleons} - \text{Mass of nucleus}$

$\Delta m = 210.741265 - 208.980388 = 1.760877 \, u$

The total binding energy ($BE$) is:

$BE = \Delta m \times 931 \, \text{MeV}$

$BE = 1.760877 \times 931 = 1639.376 \, \text{MeV}$

The binding energy per nucleon is:

$\dfrac{BE}{A} = \dfrac{1639.376}{209} \approx 7.84 \, \text{MeV}$

Answer: $7.84$

42584.subject: Physics
42584.text: A nucleus of mass $M$ emits $\gamma$-ray photon of frequency $v$. The loss of internal energy by the nucleus is: [Take $c$ as the speed of electromagnetic wave]
42584.sol:
Energy of $\gamma$ ray $\left[{E}_{\gamma}\right] = hv$

Momentum of $\gamma$ ray $\left[{P}_{\gamma}\right] = \dfrac{h}{\lambda} = \dfrac{hv}{c}$
Total momentum is conserved.

$\overset{\to}{P}\gamma + \overset{\to}{P}Nu = 0$
where $\overset{\to}{P}Nu =$ momentum of decayed nuclei

$⇒ {P}_{\gamma} = {P}_{Nu}$
$⇒ \dfrac{hv}{c} = {P}_{Nu}$
$⇒ KE$ of nuclei

$= \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} = \dfrac{{\left({P}_{Nu}\right)}^{2}}{2M} = \dfrac{1}{2M}{\left[\dfrac{hv}{c}\right]}^{2}$
Loss in internal energy $= {E}_{\gamma} + {KE}_{Nu}$
$= hv + \dfrac{1}{2M}{\left[\dfrac{hv}{c}\right]}^{2}$
$= hv\left[1 + \dfrac{hv}{2M{c}^{2}}\right]$

42717.subject: Physics
42717.text: The metallic bob of simple pendulum has the relative density $5$. The time period of this pendulum is $10s$. If the metallic bob is immersed in water, then the new time period becomes $5\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
42717.sol:
When the bob is immersed in water its effective weight is $m{g}^{'} = mg - {F}_{B}$, where, ${F}_{B}$ is buoyant force.

Then, ${g}^{'} = \dfrac{mg - {F}_{B}}{m}$ $= \dfrac{{ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{W}Vg}{{ρ}_{B}V}$

$= \left(\dfrac{{ρ}_{B} - {ρ}_{w}}{{ρ}_{B}}\right)g$ $= \dfrac{5 - 1}{5} \times g$$= \dfrac{4}{5}g$

Now, time period of simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

Thus, the ratio $\dfrac{{T}^{'}}{T} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{{g}^{'}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\dfrac{4}{5}g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}}$

$⇒ {T}^{'} = T\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{10}{2}\sqrt{5}$

Thus, the new time period is ${T}^{'} = 5\sqrt{5}s$.

Hence, value of $x = 5$.

49363.text: Probability of at least one of the events A and B occur is $0.6$. If A and B occur simultaneously with probability $0.2$, then $P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B})$ is
49363.sol:
Given $P(A \cup B) = 0.6$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0.2$.

Using the addition theorem of probability:

$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$

$0.6 = P(A) + P(B) - 0.2$

$P(A) + P(B) = 0.8$

We need to find $P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B})$:

$P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B}) = (1 - P(A)) + (1 - P(B))$

$P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B}) = 2 - (P(A) + P(B))$

$P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B}) = 2 - 0.8 = 1.2$

Answer: $1.2$

Pur $f^{\prime}(x)=0$, for maxima or minima, we get $\log x-1=0\Rightarrow \quad x=e$ Now, $f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{(\log x)^2 \cdot \frac{1}{x}-(\log x-1) \cdot \frac{2 \log x}{x}}{(\log x)^4}\Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime \prime}(e)=\frac{\frac{1}{e}-0}{1}=\frac{1}{e}>0\therefore$ Function is minimum at $x=e$. Hence, minimum value of $f(x)$ at $x=e$ is $f(e)=e .$

54886.subject: Chemistry
54886.text: Which of the following forms 2-Methylbut-2-ene on heating with concentrated sulphuric acid?
54886.sol:
Target Product: 2-Methylbut-2-ene
$\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3}$

Dehydration of alcohols with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ proceeds via an E1 mechanism, forming carbocations that undergo elimination following Zaitsev's rule.

Butan-2-ol yields but-2-ene as the major product, not the target compound. 2-Methyl-2-propanol dehydrates to form 2-methylpropene.

2-Methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol undergoes dehydration with carbocation rearrangement: the primary carbocation $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2+}$ rearranges via 1,2-hydride shift to form the tertiary carbocation $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C+(CH_3)-CH_3}$. Elimination produces both 2-methylbut-1-ene and 2-methylbut-2-ene, with the latter being the major product.

2-Methylbutan-2-ol forms the same tertiary carbocation directly without rearrangement, then eliminates to yield 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product.

While both C and D produce the target alkene, tertiary alcohols like 2-methylbutan-2-ol undergo dehydration more readily and without rearrangement, making it the most direct precursor.

56347.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
56347.text: Which element from following has positive electron gain enthalpy?
56347.sol:
Electron gain enthalpy is the enthalpy change when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom.

Halogens such as Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine have a strong tendency to accept an electron to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, resulting in highly negative electron gain enthalpies.

Noble gases like Xenon have a completely filled and stable valence shell (ns^2 np^6$). Adding an electron requires energy to place it in a higher energy principal quantum shell, overcoming interelectronic repulsions. Thus, Xenon has a positive electron gain enthalpy.

Answer: Xenon$

57966.subject: Chemistry
57966.text: The solubility of a sparingly soluble a salt $\text{AB}_2$ is $1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{mol/dm}^3$. Calculate its solubility product?
57966.sol:
The dissociation of the salt $AB_2$ is given by:

$AB_2 \rightleftharpoons A^{2+} + 2B^-$

Let the solubility of the salt be $S$. The equilibrium concentrations are:

$[A^{2+}] = S$

$[B^-] = 2S$

The solubility product $K_{sp}$ is:

$K_{sp} = [A^{2+}][B^-]^2$

$K_{sp} = (S)(2S)^2 = 4S^3$

Given $S = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{mol/dm}^3$, substituting this value:

$K_{sp} = 4(1 \times 10^{-6})^3$

$K_{sp} = 4 \times 10^{-18}$

Answer: $4 \times 10^{-18}$

57970.subject: Chemistry
57970.text: The solubility of sapringly soluble salt $\text{AB}_2$ is $18 \cdot 78 \times 10^{-4} \text{ g/dm}^3$ What is its solubility product ? (Molar mass of $\text{AB}_2 = 187 \cdot 8 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
57970.sol:
Solubility $S$ in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ is calculated by dividing the solubility in $\text{g dm}^{-3}$ by the molar mass.

$S = \dfrac{18 \cdot 78 \times 10^{-4}}{187 \cdot 8} = 10^{-5} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$

The dissociation of the salt $\text{AB}_2$ is given by:

$\text{AB}_2 \rightleftharpoons \textA^{2+} + 2\textB^{-}$

The solubility product $K_{sp}$ is:

$K_{sp} = [\textA^{2+}][\textB^{-}]^2 = (S)(2S)^2 = 4S^3$

Substituting the value of $S$:

$K_{sp} = 4 \times (10^{-5})^3 = 4 \times 10^{-15}$

Answer: $4 \times 10^{-15}$

59922.subject: Chemistry
59922.text: Which from following transformations is endothermic in nature?
59922.sol:
Endothermic processes absorb energy, indicated by positive enthalpy change ($\Delta H > 0$), while exothermic processes release energy ($\Delta H < 0$).

Freezing ($\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(s)}$) releases energy as molecules form ordered structures.

Melting ($\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}$) requires energy absorption to overcome intermolecular forces.

Condensation ($\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}$) and deposition ($\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{s})}$) both release energy during phase transition to more condensed states.

Only melting exhibits endothermic behavior.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

62740.subject: Mathematics
62740.sol:
To evaluate the limit $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{|x|}{|x| + x^2}$, we consider left and right limits due to the absolute value.

For $x \to 0^+$ where $x > 0$ and $|x| = x$, the expression becomes $\frac{x}{x + x^2}$. Canceling $x$ gives $\frac{1}{1 + x}$, which approaches $1$.

For $x \to 0^-$ where $x < 0$ and $|x| = -x$, the expression becomes $\frac{-x}{-x + x^2}$. Canceling $-x$ yields $\frac{1}{1 - x}$, which also approaches $1$.

Since both limits equal $1$, the limit exists and is $1$.

The answer is B.

62931.subject: Mathematics
62931.text:
The correct logical equivalence from the following is /are ___
(I) $p \to (q \to r) \equiv (p \wedge q) \to r$
(II) $(p \to q) \to r \equiv p \to (q \vee r)$
(III) $(p \to q) \to r \equiv (p \to r) \wedge (\sim q \to r)$
(IV) $p \to (q \to r) \equiv q \to (p \to r)$
62931.sol:
Using the property $A \to B \equiv \sim A \vee B$, we evaluate each statement.

For (I):
$p \to (q \to r) \equiv \sim p \vee (\sim q \vee r) \equiv (\sim p \vee \sim q) \vee r \equiv \sim(p \wedge q) \vee r \equiv (p \wedge q) \to r$
Statement (I) is correct.

For (II):
$(p \to q) \to r \equiv (\sim p \vee q) \to r \equiv \sim(\sim p \vee q) \vee r \equiv (p \wedge \sim q) \vee r \equiv (p \vee r) \wedge (\sim q \vee r)$
$p \to (q \vee r) \equiv \sim p \vee q \vee r$
Statement (II) is incorrect.

For (III):
$(p \to q) \to r \equiv (p \vee r) \wedge (\sim q \vee r)$
$(p \to r) \wedge (\sim q \to r) \equiv (\sim p \vee r) \wedge (q \vee r)$
Statement (III) is incorrect.

For (IV):
$p \to (q \to r) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q \vee r$
$q \to (p \to r) \equiv \sim q \vee (\sim p \vee r) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q \vee r$
Statement (IV) is correct.

Therefore, only (I) and (IV) are correct.

Answer: only (I) and (IV)

64355.subject: Mathematics
64355.text: From a point P $(a, b, c)$, perpendiculars PA and PB are drawn to XY plane and ZX plane respectively. If O is the origin, then the equation of plane OAB is
64355.sol:
The coordinates of point P are $(a, b, c)$.

Since PA is perpendicular to the XY plane, the $z$-coordinate of A is $0$. Thus, the coordinates of A are $(a, b, 0)$.

Since PB is perpendicular to the ZX plane, the $y$-coordinate of B is $0$. Thus, the coordinates of B are $(a, 0, c)$.

The equation of the plane passing through the origin O $(0, 0, 0)$, A $(a, b, 0)$, and B $(a, 0, c)$ is given by:

$\begin{vmatrix} x \text{ and } y \text{ and } z \\ a \text{ and } b \text{ and } 0 \\ a \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } c \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row, we get:

$x(bc - 0) - y(ac - 0) + z(0 - ab) = 0$

$bcx - acy - abz = 0$

Dividing the entire equation by $abc$, we get:

$\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{y}{b} - \dfrac{z}{c} = 0$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{y}{b} - \dfrac{z}{c} = 0$

65158.text: If $\bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}, \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ then a vector $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ such that $\bar{a} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}=\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\bar{a} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=3$ is
65158.sol:
Finding vector $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ from given conditions:

Let $\overline{\mathrm{c}} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$. Given $\bar{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{b}} = \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, with $\bar{a} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}} = 3$ and $\bar{a} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}} = \overline{\mathrm{b}}$.

The dot product yields $\bar{a} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}} = x + y + z = 3$.

The cross product $\bar{a} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ evaluates to $(z - y)\hat{i} - (z - x)\hat{j} + (y - x)\hat{k}$, which equals $\overline{\mathrm{b}} = 0\hat{i} + 1\hat{j} - 1\hat{k}$. Component comparison gives $z = y$, $x - z = 1$, and $y - x = -1$.

Substituting $y = z$ into the dot product: $x + 2z = 3$. With $x - z = 1$, subtracting yields $3z = 2$, so $z = \frac{2}{3}$ and $x = \frac{5}{3}$. Since $y = z$, $y = \frac{2}{3}$.

Thus, $\overline{\mathrm{c}} = \frac{5}{3}\hat{i} + \frac{2}{3}\hat{j} + \frac{2}{3}\hat{k}$, matching option A.

Final answer is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

66779.subject: Physics
66779.text: The following figure represents two bulbs $B_1$ and $B_2$, resistor R and an inductor L. When the switch S is turned off, which of the following statement is true?
options: $B_1$ becomes off promptly but $B_2$ with some delay
$B_2$ becomes off promptly but $B_1$ with some delay
Both $B_1$ and $B_2$ becomes off with same delay
66779.sol:
When the switch S is turned off, the main voltage source is disconnected from the circuit.

The inductor L has stored energy in its magnetic field. According to Faraday's and Lenz's laws, it opposes the sudden drop in current and acts as a source of emf.

A closed loop is formed containing the inductor L, bulb $B_2$, bulb $B_1$, and resistor R in series.

The induced current from the inductor flows through this series loop, meaning the same decaying current passes through both bulbs $B_1$ and $B_2$.

Since the current through both bulbs is identical at any instant after the switch is opened, both $B_1$ and $B_2$ become off with the same delay.

66812.text: Initially a rectangular coil with length vertical is moving out with constant velocity 'v' in a constant magnetic field 'B' towards right. Now the same coil is rotated through $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ in same plane in same magnetic field $B$ and the coil is moving with same velocity $v$. The magnitude of induced e.m.f. is now
options: sometimes greater and sometimes less than initial induced e.m.f.
66812.sol:
For a conductor moving perpendicular to a magnetic field, the induced e.m.f. is governed by $\varepsilon = B l v$, where $l$ is the length cutting flux lines perpendicularly.

The rectangular coil has dimensions $L$ (length) and $w$ (width). Initially, with $L$ vertical, the induced e.m.f. is $\varepsilon_{\text{initial}} = B L v$.

After a $90^{}^{\circ}$ rotation, the vertical side becomes $w$, so $\varepsilon_{\text{final}} = B w v$.

The magnitudes compare as $\varepsilon_{\text{final}} > \varepsilon_{\text{initial}}$ if $w > L$, $\varepsilon_{\text{final}} < \varepsilon_{\text{initial}}$ if $w < L$, and are equal if $w = L$. Since no dimensions are specified, all outcomes are possible, leading to answer $\boxed{D}$.

68098.subject: Physics
68098.text: One large soap bubble of diameter 'D' breaks into $64$ bubbles having surface tension 'T'. The change in surface energy is
68098.sol:
Let $R$ be the radius of the large bubble and $r$ be the radius of each small bubble.

Equating the initial and final volumes:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 64 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

$R^3 = 64 r^3 \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{4}$

A soap bubble has two free surfaces. The initial surface energy is:

$U_i = T \times 2 \times 4\pi R^2 = 8\pi R^2 T$

The final surface energy of $64$ small bubbles is:

$U_f = 64 \times T \times 2 \times 4\pi r^2 = 512\pi r^2 T$

Substituting $r = \dfrac{R}{4}$:

$U_f = 512\pi \left(\dfrac{R}{4}\right)^2 T = 512\pi \dfrac{R^2}{16} T = 32\pi R^2 T$

The change in surface energy is:

$\Delta U = U_f - U_i = 32\pi R^2 T - 8\pi R^2 T = 24\pi R^2 T$

Given the diameter $D = 2R$, we substitute $R = \dfrac{D}{2}$:

$\Delta U = 24\pi \left(\dfrac{D}{2}\right)^2 T = 24\pi \dfrac{D^2}{4} T = 6\pi TD^2$

Answer: $6\pi TD^2$

70220.subject: Physics
70220.text: A plate of refractive index 1.6 is introduced in the path of light from one of the slits in Young's double slit experiment then
options: the fringe width towards the side of the plate will decrease.
the central maximum will shift towards this side
number of fringes seen will decrease.
70220.sol:
When a thin plate of refractive index \(n\) is introduced in front of one of the slits in Young's double-slit experiment, it adds an extra optical path (and hence a phase difference) to the light coming from that slit. This shifts the entire interference pattern on the screen but does not change the fringe spacing or make the pattern disappear.
Fringe width does not change because it depends on the slit separation and the wavelength in air, not on a uniform phase shift introduced in one path.
Number of visible fringes does not necessarily decrease (as long as the plate is not too thick to cause excessive absorption or other effects).
The interference pattern does not vanish unless coherence is destroyed (e.g., by scattering or large thickness variations).
The net effect of introducing a uniform optical path difference in one slit is a lateral shift of the central maximum (and all fringes) toward the slit with the plate.
Hence the correct statement is :
(B) The central maximum will shift towards the side on which the plate is introduced.

70434.text: An air column in a pipe which is closed at one end will be in resonance with a vibrating tuning fork of frequency 415 Hz for various vibrating air columns. Which one of the following lengths is not in resonance ? (velocity of sound in air = 332 m/s) (Neglect end correction)
70434.sol:
Given frequency $f = 415 \text{ Hz}$ and velocity $v = 332 \text{ m/s}$.

The wavelength of the sound wave is:

$\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{332}{415} \text{ m}$

$\lambda = 0.8 \text{ m} = 80 \text{ cm}$

For a pipe closed at one end, the resonating lengths are given by odd multiples of $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$:

$L = (2n - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$

The possible resonating lengths are:

$L_1 = 1 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 20 \text{ cm}$

$L_2 = 3 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 60 \text{ cm}$

$L_3 = 5 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 100 \text{ cm}$

Among the given options, $40 \text{ cm}$ is an even multiple of $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ and therefore is not a resonating length.

71074.subject: Biology
71074.text: Similarity of bone structure in the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of __________.
71074.sol:
Similarity of bone structure in the forelimbs of many vertebrates, such as whales, bats, cheetahs, and humans, is a classic example of homologous organs.

These organs share a common anatomical plan and embryonic origin but have been modified to perform different functions in different animals, such as swimming, flying, running, and grasping.

This phenomenon indicates divergent evolution, where a common ancestral structure has evolved in different directions to adapt to various environmental needs.

Answer: homologous organs

71170.subject: Biology
71170.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I - The external genitalia of female contains two thin folds called labia majora which forms hood-like covering around clitoris.
Statement II - The vestibular glands are homologous to the Cowper's gland of the male reproductive system.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
71170.sol:
Statement I is incorrect because the labia majora are fleshy folds of tissue that extend down from the mons pubis and surround the vaginal opening. The labia minora are paired thin folds of tissue under the labia majora, and it is the labia minora that form the hood-like covering (prepuce) around the clitoris.

Statement II is correct because the greater vestibular glands (Bartholin's glands) in females are homologous to the bulbourethral glands (Cowper's glands) in the male reproductive system. Both secrete mucus for lubrication.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.

71255.subject: Biology
71255.text: Two different amino acids will never be encoded by the same codon, which property of genetic code does this represent?
71255.sol:
The genetic code is unambiguous and specific, which means that one codon codes for only one specific amino acid. It will never code for two different amino acids.

Degeneracy refers to the property where a single amino acid can be coded by multiple different codons.

Non-overlapping means that the sequence of bases is read in discrete sets of three, without any overlap between adjacent codons.

Therefore, the statement that two different amino acids will never be encoded by the same codon represents the non-ambiguous nature of the genetic code.

Answer: Code in non-ambiguous

72256.subject: Physics
72256.text: A long straight wire along the $z$-axis carries a current '$I$' in the negative z-direction. The magnetic induction '$\vec{B}$' at a point having co-ordinates $(x, y)$ on the $z = 0$ plane is
72256.sol:
The magnetic field due to a long straight wire carrying current $I$ is given by:

$\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d} (\hat{u} \times \hat{n})$

where $\hat{u}$ is the unit vector along the direction of current, $d$ is the perpendicular distance from the wire, and $\hat{n}$ is the unit vector along the position vector of the point with respect to the wire.

Since the current is in the negative z-direction, $\hat{u} = -\hat{k}$.

The position vector of the point $(x, y)$ on the $z = 0$ plane is $\vec{r} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}$.

The distance of the point from the wire is $d = |\vec{r}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$.

The unit vector $\hat{n} = \dfrac{\vec{r}}{|\vec{r}|} = \dfrac{x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}$.

Substituting these values:

$\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}} \left( -\hat{k} \times \dfrac{x\hat{i} + y\hat{j}}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}} \right)

\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (x^2 + y^2)} (-$ x(\hat{k} $\times \hat{i}) -$ y(\hat{k} $\times \hat{j}))

Using the standard cross products \hat{k} \times \hat{i} = \hat{j} and \hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}:

\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (x^2 + y^2)} (-$ x\hat{j} - y(-\hat{i}))$

\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I (y\hat{i} - x\hat{j})}{2\pi (x² + y²)}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 I(y\hat{i} - x\hat{j})}{2\pi(x² + y²)}$

72358.text: An object is placed 15 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm, then the nature of the image formed will be
72358.sol:
Given object distance $u = -15$ cm and focal length $f = -10$ cm.

Using the mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{15} = -\dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{2 - 3}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{30}$

$v = -30$ cm

Magnification $m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{-30}{-15} = -2$

Since $m$ is negative, the image is real and inverted. Since $|m| > 1$, the image is magnified.

Answer: magnified and inverted

73787.subject: General Ability
73787.text: A glass slab of refractive index $1.5$ is cut in the shape of a parallelepiped $ABCD$ as shown in the figure. Surface $BC$ is polished to form a perfect reflector. Light is incident at surface $AB$ from inside at an angle $\pi/3$. Which one of the following is the correct angle $ABC$ $(\theta)$ such that the reflected light retraces its path?
73787.sol:
For the reflected light to retrace its path, it must strike the polished surface $BC$ normally (perpendicularly). This means the angle between the reflected ray and surface $BC$ must be $90^{\circ}$.

Assuming the given angle $\pi/3$ ($60^{\circ}$) is the angle the incident ray makes with the surface $AB$, by the law of reflection, the reflected ray will also make an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the surface $AB$.

Consider the triangle formed by the point of incidence on $AB$, the point of normal incidence on $BC$, and the vertex $B$. The sum of the internal angles in this triangle must be $180^{\circ}$.

The angle between the reflected ray and surface $AB$ is $60^{\circ}$.
The angle between the reflected ray and surface $BC$ is $90^{\circ}$.

Therefore, the angle $\theta$ (angle $ABC$) is:
$\theta = 180^{\circ} - (90^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}) = 30^{\circ}$

Converting $30^{\circ}$ to radians, we get $\theta = \pi/6$.

73929.subject: General Ability
73929.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Diamond is hard due to extended covalent bonding in it
Fullerene is composed of five and six membered rings
Diamond is a good conductor of electricity
Graphite is used as a lubricant
73929.sol:
In diamond, each carbon atom is $sp^3$ hybridized and covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms, forming a rigid three-dimensional network. Since all four valence electrons of each carbon atom are localized in these strong covalent bonds, there are no free electrons available to conduct electricity. Thus, diamond is an insulator, not a good conductor of electricity.

The other statements are correct:
Diamond is extremely hard due to its extended three-dimensional covalent bonding.
Fullerenes (like $C_{60}$) are composed of both five-membered and six-membered carbon rings.
Graphite has a layered structure with weak van der Waals forces between the layers, allowing them to slide over one another, making it an excellent solid lubricant.

Answer: Diamond is a good conductor of electricity

75184.text: As per the Land Revenue Records, any land is categorized as Culturable Waste-Land if it is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than
75184.sol:
According to the Land Revenue Records in India, land use categories are defined based on the duration for which the land is left uncultivated.

Current fallow land is left uncultivated for one or less than one agricultural year.

Fallow land other than current fallow is left uncultivated for the past 1 to 5 agricultural years.

Culturable waste-land is defined as any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than 5 agricultural years. It can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.

Answer: 5 years

Given that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the equation
$\begin{array}{cl} & x^2-a x-b x+a b-c=0 \\ \text{ i.e } & x^2-(a+b) x+a b-c=0 \\ \therefore & \alpha+\beta=a+b \quad \alpha . \beta=a b-c \\ \Rightarrow & a b=\alpha \beta+c\end{array}$
The quadratic equation whose roots are $a and b$ is
 $\begin{aligned}& x²-(a+b) x+a b=0 \\ & x²-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha \beta+c=0 \\ & x²-\alphax-\betax+\alpha \beta+c=0\end{aligned}$

83450.subject: Physics
83450.text: The ratio of the radii of gyration of a circular disc to that of a circular ring, each of same mass and radius, around their respective axes is
83450.sol:
Key Idea : The square root of the ratio of the moment of inertia of a rigid body and its mass is called radius of gyration.
As in key idea, radius of gyration is given by
$K=\sqrt{\frac{I}{M}}$
For given problem
$\frac{K_{\text{disc }}}{K_{\text{ring }}}=\sqrt{\frac{I_{\text{disc }}}{I_{\text{ring }}}}$
But $I_{\text{disc }}$ (about its axis) $=\frac{1}{2} M R^2$ and $I_{\text{ring }}$ (about its axis) $=M R^2$ where $R$ is the radius of both bodies. Therefore, Eq. (i) becomes
$\frac{K_{\mathrm{disc}}}{K_{\text{ring }}}=\sqrt{\frac{\frac{1}{2} M R^2}{M R^2}}=1: \sqrt{2}$

84171.sol:

84735.subject: Zoology
84735.text: Select the correct statement with respect to disorders of muscles in humans.
options: Failure of neuromuscular transmission in myasthenia gravis can prevent normal swallowing.
Accumulation of urea and creatine in the joints causes their inflammation.
An overdose of vitamin D causes osteoporosis.
Rapid contractions of skeletal muscles cause muscle dystrophy.
84735.sol:
Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder in which autoantibodies bind to cholinergic receptors on muscle cells and impairs the ability of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine to induce muscular contraction. This leads to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscles of mouth and throat which may prevent normal swallowing.
Gout arthritis is caused due to excessive formation of uric acid. It gets deposited in synovial joints and causes inflammation. Ostcoporosis is a discase in which bone loses minerals and fibres from its matrix. Muscular dystrophy is inborn abnormality of muscles associated with dysfunction and ultimately with deterioration.
Related Theory
Autoimmune diseases are a group of disorders in which tissue injury is caused by humoral (autoantibodies) or cell-mediated (by autoreactive $T$ cells) immune response to self-antigens.

85342.text: Nicotiana sylvestris flowers only during long days and N.tabacum flowers only during short days. If raised in the laboratory under different photoperiods, they can be indued to flower at the same time and can be cross-fertilized to produce self-fertile offspring. What is the best reason considering $N$. sylvestris and N.tabocum to be separate species ?
85342.sol:
According to biological species concept, a species is a natural inbreeding group which may have essentially similar morphological traits but they are genetically distinct and reproductively isolated from others. As under laboratory conditions, N. tabacum and $\mathrm{N}$. sylvestris cannot produce selffertile offspring, so they are not reproductively isolated. They are considered as separate species because since their flowering periods are different so cross pollination is not possible between them naturally. This makes them different species.

The partial pressure of the reactant and product are denoted, respectively, by $p_{reactant}$ and $p_{product}$ during the course of the reactions. Assuming ideal gas behaviour, the correct plot of $p_{reactant}$ versus $p_{product}$ for Experiments I and II is:
86027.sol:
Let the initial partial pressure of reactant $X$ be $P_0$.

For Experiment I, $X(g) \rightleftharpoons 2Y(g)$. If the partial pressure of $X$ decreases by $x$, then the partial pressure of product $Y$ increases by $2x$.

We have $p_{\text{reactant}} = P_0 - x$ and $p_{\text{product}} = 2x$, which gives $x = \dfrac{p_{\text{product}}}{2}$.

Substituting this into the first equation, we get $p_{\text{reactant}} = P_0 - \dfrac{1}{2}p_{\text{product}}$. This represents a straight line with a slope of $-1/2$ and an x-intercept of $2P_0$.

For Experiment II, $X(g) \rightleftharpoons Z(g)$. If the partial pressure of $X$ decreases by $y$, then the partial pressure of product $Z$ increases by $y$.

We have $p_{\text{reactant}} = P_0 - y$ and $p_{\text{product}} = y$.

Substituting $y$, we get $p_{\text{reactant}} = P_0 - p_{\text{product}}$. This represents a straight line with a slope of $-1$ and an x-intercept of $P_0$.

Both equations are linear, so the plots must be straight lines. The line for Experiment II has a steeper negative slope ($-1$) compared to Experiment I ($-1/2$) and intersects the x-axis at a smaller value ($P_0$ vs $2P_0$). This correctly corresponds to the graph shown in option (4).

Answer :

101011.text: A point mass of $1$ kg moving horizontally with speed $u$ hits a pendulum bob of mass $2$ kg initially at rest. The collision is perfectly elastic. After the collision, the pendulum bob swings upwards and reaches a maximum vertical height of $0.8$ m. Taking $g = 10$ ms$^{-2}$, the initial speed $u$ of the $1$ kg mass is:
101011.sol:
First, find the velocity of the $2$ kg bob just after the collision using conservation of mechanical energy during its upward swing:

$\dfrac{1}{2} M v_M^2 = M g h$

$v_M = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.8} = \sqrt{16} = 4$ ms$^{-1}$.

For a 1D elastic collision, the velocity of a target mass $M$ initially at rest, struck by a mass $m$ moving with initial velocity $u$, is given by:

$v_M = \dfrac{2m}{m + M} u$

Substituting the given values ($m = 1$ kg, $M = 2$ kg, $v_M = 4$ ms$^{-1}$):

$4 = \dfrac{2 \times 1}{1 + 2} u$

$4 = \dfrac{2}{3} u$

$u = 6$ ms$^{-1}$.

Answer: $6$ ms$^{-1}$

101703.subject: Physics
101703.text: Two spherical raindrops of masses $m$ and $8m$ fall through the air. Assuming the density of the raindrops is uniform and neglecting the buoyant force of air, the ratio of their terminal velocities is:
101703.sol:
Let the radii of the two raindrops be $r_1$ and $r_2$.

Since the density $\rho$ is the same for both raindrops, mass $m = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho$.

Therefore, $m \propto r^3$.

Given the ratio of masses is $m : 8m = 1 : 8$, the ratio of their radii is:

$\dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \left( \dfrac{1}{8} \right)^{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The terminal velocity $v$ of a spherical drop falling through a viscous medium is given by Stokes' law:

$v = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$

Thus, terminal velocity $v \propto r^2$.

The ratio of their terminal velocities is:

$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \left( \dfrac{r_1}{r_2} \right)^2 = \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Hence, the ratio is $1 : 4$.

Answer: $1 : 4$

102074.subject: Physics
102074.text: An ideal gas undergoes a clockwise cyclic process consisting of three steps. The states of the gas at the vertices of the cycle on a $P-V$ diagram are $(V_0, 2P_0)$, $(3V_0, 2P_0)$, and $(V_0, P_0)$. What is the ratio of the work done by the gas during the isobaric expansion segment to the net work done by the gas in the entire cycle?
102074.sol:
The cyclic process forms a right-angled triangle on the $P-V$ diagram.

The isobaric expansion occurs at a constant pressure of $2P_0$ from volume $V_0$ to $3V_0$.
Work done during this expansion, $W_{exp} = P \Delta V = 2P_0(3V_0 - V_0) = 4P_0V_0$.

The net work done in the clockwise cycle is the area of the triangle enclosed on the $P-V$ diagram.
Base of the triangle (change in volume) = $3V_0 - V_0 = 2V_0$.
Height of the triangle (change in pressure) = $2P_0 - P_0 = P_0$.
Net work, $W_{net} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2V_0 \times P_0 = P_0V_0$.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{W_{exp}}{W_{net}} = \dfrac{4P_0V_0}{P_0V_0} = 4$.

Answer: $4$

102244.subject: Physics
102244.text: A certain amount of a non-linear polyatomic gas having $f$ active vibrational modes undergoes an isobaric expansion. If $Q$ is the heat supplied to the gas and $W$ is the work done by the gas, the ratio $\dfrac{W}{Q}$ is:
102244.sol:
For a non-linear polyatomic gas, the number of translational degrees of freedom is 3 and rotational degrees of freedom is 3.

Each active vibrational mode contributes $R$ to the molar heat capacity at constant volume ($C_v$).

Thus, $C_v = \dfrac{3}{2}R + \dfrac{3}{2}R + fR = (3+f)R$

The molar heat capacity at constant pressure is:
$C_p = C_v + R = (4+f)R$

In an isobaric process, the work done by the gas is $W = nR\Delta T$ and the heat supplied is $Q = nC_p\Delta T$.

Therefore, the ratio is:
$\dfrac{W}{Q} = \dfrac{nR\Delta T}{nC_p\Delta T} = \dfrac{R}{C_p} = \dfrac{R}{(4+f)R} = \dfrac{1}{4+f}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4+f}$

103023.text: If the electric flux entering and leaving an enclosed surface respectively are $\phi$, and $\phi_2$, the electric charge inside the surface will be
103023.sol:
According to Gauss theorem "the net electric flux through any closed surface is equal to the net charge inside the surface divided by $\varepsilon_0{ }^{\prime \prime}$.
Therefore, $\quad \phi \propto \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}$
Let $-q_1$ be the charge, due to which flux $\phi_1$ is entering the surface,
$\phi_1=\frac{-q_1}{\varepsilon_0} -q_1=\varepsilon_0 \phi_1$
Let $+q_2$ be the charge, due to which flux $\phi_2$ is entering the surface.
$\phi_2=\frac{q_2}{\varepsilon_0}
or \quad q_2=\varepsilon_0 \phi_2$
So, electric charge inside the surface
$=q_2-q_1 \begin{aligned} & =\varepsilon_0 \phi_2+\varepsilon_0 \phi_1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad=\varepsilon_0\left(\phi_2+\phi_1\right) \end{aligned}$

107730.subject: Chemistry
107730.text: In the ground state of an oxygen ($O_2$) molecule, the unpaired electrons occupy specific molecular orbitals. Which of the following correctly describes the nature and symmetry of these molecular orbitals with respect to the internuclear axis?
options: They are antibonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals, which are unsymmetrical around the internuclear axis.
They are antibonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals, which are symmetrical around the internuclear axis.
They are antibonding $\sigma$ molecular orbitals, which are symmetrical around the internuclear axis.
They are bonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals, which are unsymmetrical around the internuclear axis.
107730.sol:
The electronic configuration of an $O_2$ molecule (16 electrons) according to Molecular Orbital Theory is:
$\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^{*} 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^{*} 2s^2 \sigma 2p_z^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2) (\pi^{*} 2p_x^1 = \pi^{*} 2p_y^1)$

The two unpaired electrons are present in the $\pi^{*} 2p_x$ and $\pi^{*} 2p_y$ molecular orbitals.

These are antibonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals. According to MOT, all $\pi$ molecular orbitals (both bonding and antibonding) have zero electron density along the internuclear axis and are unsymmetrical around the internuclear axis.

Therefore, the unpaired electrons occupy antibonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals that are unsymmetrical around the internuclear axis.

Answer: They are antibonding $\pi$ molecular orbitals, which are unsymmetrical around the internuclear axis.

117793.subject: Chemistry
117793.text: A coordination compound with the empirical formula $\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{BrSO}_4$ exists in two isomeric forms, A and B. When an aqueous solution of form A is treated with $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ solution, a white precipitate is formed. When an aqueous solution of form B is treated with $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ solution, a pale yellow precipitate is formed. The type of structural isomerism exhibited by forms A and B is:
117793.sol:
The formation of a white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl}_2$ indicates the presence of free sulphate ions ($\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$) in the solution. This means form A has sulphate outside the coordination sphere: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{Br}\right]\mathrm{SO}_4$.

The formation of a pale yellow precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ indicates the presence of free bromide ions ($\mathrm{Br}^-$) in the solution. This means form B has bromide outside the coordination sphere: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5\mathrm{SO}_4\right]\mathrm{Br}$.

Since forms A and B differ in the distribution of ions between the coordination sphere and the ionisation sphere, they exhibit ionisation isomerism.

Answer: Ionisation isomerism

121812.subject: Botany
121812.text: What true structures do Pteridophytes possess?
121812.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. <mark>In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves</mark> (Figure 3.3). These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. The leaves in pteridophytes are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns. The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum). The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells.

122591.sol:
Let us evaluate each option based on their classification:

Fasciola (Platyhelminthes) exhibits an organ level of body organization, not organ-system level. It is bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate.

Ascaris (Aschelminthes) has an organ-system level of organization and bilateral symmetry, but it is pseudocoelomate, not coelomate.

122735.subject: Botany
122735.text: What type of symmetry does a mustard flower have?
122735.sol: In symmetry, the flower may be actinomorphic (radial symmetry) or zygomorphic (bilateral symmetry). When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre, it is said to be actinomorphic, e.g., mustard, datura, chilli. When it can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia. A flower is asymmetric (irregular) if it cannot be divided into two similar halves by any vertical plane passing through the centre, as in canna.

123573.subject: Botany
123573.text: Does the number of chromosomes change during the S phase?
123573.sol: DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

124027.subject: Botany
124027.text: What is the function of vacuole in plant cells?
options: To store water and other materials
124027.sol:
Explanation: The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm. It contains water, sap, excretory product and other materials not useful for the cell. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane called tonoplast. In plant cells the vacuoles can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell. In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, hence their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.

In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.

125388.subject: Botany
125388.text: What type of phosphorylation occurs in the presence of light?
125388.sol: Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light. When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then the PS I, a process called non-cyclic photo-phosphorylation occurs. The two photosystems are connected through an electron transport chain, as seen earlier – in the Z scheme. Both ATP and NADPH + H+ are synthesised by this kind of electron flow. When only PS I is functional, the electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to cyclic flow of electrons. A possible location where this could be happening is in the stroma lamellae. While the membrane or lamellae of the grana have both PS I and PS II the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II as well as NADP reductase enzyme. The excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain (Figure 11.6). The cyclic flow hence, results only in the synthesis of ATP, but not of NADPH + H+ . Cyclic photophosphorylation also occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation.
125388.meta: What type of phosphorylation occurs in the presence of light?

125401.subject: Botany
125401.text: What measurable change occurs in the lumen due to proton accumulation?
125401.sol: The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the membrane. Along with electrons that come from the acceptor of electrons of PS I, protons are necessary for the reduction of NADP+ to NADPH+ H+ . These protons are also removed from the stroma. Hence, within the chloroplast, protons in the stroma decrease in number, while in the lumen there is accumulation of protons. This creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen. This gradient is important because it is the breakdown of this gradient that leads to the synthesis of ATP.
125401.meta: What measurable change occurs in the lumen due to proton accumulation?

125631.subject: Botany
125631.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In sugarcane, the first stable product of CO2 fixation is a 4-carbon compound.

Reason (R): Phosphoenol pyruvate (a 3-carbon compound) acts as the primary CO2 acceptor in the mesophyll cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
125631.sol:
Sugarcane is a C4 plant. In the mesophyll cells of C4 plants, the primary CO2 acceptor is Phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP), which is a 3-carbon compound.

The enzyme PEP carboxylase (PEPcase) catalyzes the addition of CO2 to PEP, forming the 4-carbon compound Oxaloacetic acid (OAA) as the first stable product.

The 3-carbon acceptor combining with 1 carbon from CO2 mathematically explains why the first stable product is a 4-carbon compound. Thus, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Assertion (A): In $C_{4}$ plants, photorespiration does not occur.
Reason (R): The breakdown of $C_{4}$ acids in the mesophyll cells releases $CO_{2}$, increasing its intracellular concentration at the enzyme site.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
125636.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. In $C_{4}$ plants, photorespiration does not occur because they possess a mechanism that increases the concentration of $CO_{2}$ at the enzyme site.

Reason (R) is incorrect. The increase in $CO_{2}$ concentration takes place when the $C_{4}$ acid (such as malic acid or aspartic acid) from the mesophyll is broken down in the bundle sheath cells, not in the mesophyll cells. This release of $CO_{2}$ in the bundle sheath cells ensures that RuBisCO functions primarily as a carboxylase, thereby minimizing its oxygenase activity.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

125878.subject: Botany
125878.text: Which type of agents do the majority of plants use for pollination?
125878.sol: Agents of Pollination: Plants use two abiotic (wind and water) and one biotic (animals) agents to achieve pollination. Majority of plants use biotic agents for pollination. Only a small proportion of plants use abiotic agents. .Pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination. To compensate for this uncertainties and associated loss of pollen grains, the flowers produce enormous amount of pollen when compared to the number of ovules available for pollination. Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollinations. Wind pollination also requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents.

125896.subject: Botany
125896.text: What happens to the male flowers of Vallisneria during pollination?
options: They are carried away by insects
They are released onto the surface of water
They are blown away by wind
They stick to the female flowers
125896.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants. In Vallisneria, the female flower reach the surface of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the surface of water. They are carried passively by water some of them eventually reach the female flowers and the stigma. In another group of water pollinated plants such as seagrasses, female flowers remain submerged in water and the pollen grains are released inside the water.
125896.meta: What happens to the male flowers of Vallisneria during pollination?

125927.subject: Botany
125927.text: What is the primary focus of the paragraph regarding pollen-pistil interaction?
options: The manipulation of pollen-pistil interaction by plant breeders
The environmental factors affecting pollen growth
125927.sol: In plants which shed pollen in the three-celled condition, pollen tubes carry the two male gametes from the beginning. Pollen tube, after reaching the ovary, enters the ovule through the micropyle and then enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus .Many recent studies have shown that filiform apparatus present at the micropylar part of the synergids guides the entry of pollen tube. All these events–from pollen deposition on the stigma until pollen tubes enter the ovule–are together referred to as pollen-pistil interaction. As pointed out earlier, pollen-pistil interaction is a dynamic process involving pollen recognition followed by promotion or inhibition of the pollen. The knowledge gained in this area would help the plant breeder in manipulating pollen-pistil interaction, even in incompatible pollinations, to get desired hybrids.
